subject: Aurora incident — stability covenant, corrective runbook and follow-through
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@auroraretail.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: support@auroraretail.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency + elevated 5xx yesterday — request for exec readout and corrective runbook

Vivek / Kimberly,

Thanks for joining the bridge yesterday. We saw a sustained latency spike between 13:05–13:40 PDT and a correlated increase in 5xx rate that impacted our checkout flow (roughly 18% of requests failing). Peak throughput recovered but drop in success rate caused retries and cart abandonment.

We need two things by EOD tomorrow:
- A concise post-incident packet with root-cause hypothesis + key metrics (latency P50/P95, 5xx rate, throughput)
- A proposed corrective runbook with owners and short-term mitigations (24–72h) and longer term fixes (2–6 weeks).

This incident has been escalated internally and our CTO may join an exec readout if you propose credits or a formal SLA remediation. Please include any proposed credits and a concrete schedule for fix verification.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of Platform Operations
Aurora Retail

Attachment: incident-screenshots.zip (image stubs)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@auroraretail.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + elevated 5xx yesterday — request for exec readout and corrective runbook

Tara — thank you for the clear ask and for getting us the traces. I’m very sorry for the customer impact.

Immediate steps:
- I’ve opened a high-priority post-incident packet and attached our initial metrics export (aurora_postincident_metrics_20270419.xlsx) and an initial draft of what we’re calling a "stability covenant"—a short, dated commitment with measurable verification steps.
- Kimberley is owning the verification plan and Marissa will lead the account-facing cadence and customer comms. Karthik will lead the short-term corrective sprint on serving runtime and routing policy.

Proposed timeline:
- By 10:00 PDT tomorrow: concise packet + short-term runbook for 24–72h mitigations
- By EOD +3 days: canary verification and automation to prevent recurrence
- Week 2–6: durable fixes (kernel selection tuning, caching policy updates, improved fallback routes) with weekly status to your team.

We will propose an exec readout slot for tomorrow afternoon; if that works we’ll include our initial credit proposal in that deck. I’ll schedule a 30-minute slot; Marissa — can you align availability with Tara?

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora_postincident_metrics_20270419.xlsx, stability-covenant-draft.md

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara@auroraretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 19:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + elevated 5xx yesterday — request for exec readout and corrective runbook

Quick technical note and runbook sketch — Tara, Vivek: attaching the short remediation checklist I mentioned on the bridge. High level:
- Immediate (0–24h): rollback recent routing policy tweak, enable aggressive KV prefix caching for Aurora workload, reduce batch window for this tenant.
- Near term (24–72h): deploy alternate kernel option, add a token-level throttling guard, extend trace retention for affected window.
- Mid term (2–6w): automated fallback variant, improved capacity headroom, SLO-based routing.

I created a JIRA ticket (JIRA-AUR-1245) to track the corrective sprint items and linked a working doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b-aurora-postincident-draft.

For the exec readout, please confirm whether your CTO (or another exec) would prefer a 15-min technical appendix plus a 15-min business impact summary.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: corrective-sprint-schedule.ics

From: Tara Singh <tara@auroraretail.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Brian Wu <brian@auroraretail.com>, support@auroraretail.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + elevated 5xx yesterday — request for exec readout and corrective runbook

Thanks Vivek/Kim. Our CTO Brian Wu will join the readout; he wants a short business-impact summary (revenue-at-risk estimate) and a clear verification plan. 15 + 15 sounds right.

We appreciate a written "covenant" with specific verification gates — that will help our procurement and legal teams evaluate an SLA remediation. Please include a verification checklist for our SREs to run during canary.

Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Platform Operations
Aurora Retail

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@auroraretail.com>, Brian Wu <brian@auroraretail.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Finalizing the "Stability Covenant" and runbook — exec readout invite + deliverables

Tara/Brian — below is the stability covenant we will present in the exec readout at 14:00 PDT today (calendar invite sent). We pledge the following deliverables and verification gates:

1) Packet: concise post-incident summary with P50/P95, 5xx trend, root-cause hypothesis and timeline — delivered by 11:30 PDT today.
2) Short-term mitigations (0–72h): rollback routing tweak, enable aggressive prefix KV caching, reduce tenant batch window — deployed to canary by 19:00 PDT today; verification checklist for Aurora SREs attached.
3) Canary verification: automated load at peak profile + 30% margin; metrics compare to baseline P95 and 5xx < 0.5% for 60m window.
4) Credit proposal: contingent on failed verification we will provide invoice credit equivalent to 10% of April usage for the affected window; final amount to be confirmed in follow-up.
5) Mid-term (2–6w): kernel tuning, fallback route automation, SLO-based routing policy. Weekly status update on Fridays.

Owners:
- Verification plan: kimberly_park
- Customer comms and exec scheduling: marissa_cole
- Corrective sprint execution: karthik_iyer
- Exec escalation/credits: vivek_kulkarni

Links: post-incident draft https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b-aurora-postincident-draft, JIRA-AUR-1245.

We’ll present the packet, the verification checklist, and the initial mitigation timeline in the 14:00 slot. If the canary meets the gates we’ll close the immediate remediation loop and move into the mid-term workstream. If not, we’ve agreed the invoice credit path above.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this as our highest priority until fully remediated.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: stability-covenant-draft.md, aurora_postincident_metrics_20270419.xlsx, corrective-sprint-schedule.ics
